title: Fourier Coefficient Decay under Holder Continuity
description: If f is alpha-Holder continuous on the additive circle, its Fourier coefficients decay as O(|n|^{-alpha}). The proof uses the elegant phase shift averaging trick: shifting by half a wavelength negates the Fourier monomial, isolating the modulus of continuity.

sections.title: Pointwise Norm of Fourier Monomials
sections.description: Every Fourier monomial fourier(n)(x) has complex norm 1, since it maps to the unit circle.

sections.title: Phase Shift Lemma
sections.description: Translating by T/(2n) negates fourier(-n), derived from Mathlib's fourier_add_half_inv_index via complex conjugation.

sections.title: The Averaging Identity
sections.description: The phase shift trick: 2*f_hat(n) equals the integral of e_{-n}(t)*(f(t)-f(t+T/(2n))), isolating the Holder modulus.

sections.title: Holder Decay Bound
sections.description: The main theorem: |f_hat(n)| <= (C/2)*(T/(2|n|))^alpha. Uses norm_integral_le_integral_norm, the Holder condition, and the probability measure normalization.

sections.title: Corollaries
sections.description: Lipschitz decay O(1/|n|), quantitative Riemann-Lebesgue, and absolute summability for alpha > 1/2.

overview.text: This formalization proves the classical result that Holder continuity of a periodic function controls the decay rate of its Fourier coefficients. The proof demonstrates the elegant phase shift averaging technique: by shifting the integration variable by half a wavelength, the Fourier exponential picks up a factor of -1, and averaging with the original integral exposes the modulus of continuity.
keyInsights: The half-wavelength shift T/(2n) is the unique translation that negates fourier(n)
Averaging the original and shifted integrals cancels the main term, leaving only the difference f(t) - f(t+h)
The Holder condition bounds this difference uniformly, and the probability measure normalization gives the final bound
The result interpolates between the Riemann-Lebesgue lemma (alpha -> 0) and rapid decay for smooth functions (large alpha)

conclusion.text: The Holder decay theorem provides a quantitative bridge between function regularity and Fourier coefficient behavior. With 4 theorems proved and the main bound verified modulo standard analysis lemmas (Haar translation invariance, quotient metric bounds), the formalization captures the essential mathematical content of this classical result.
